action: UK health organisations: reply to the ICO by November 27. If access controls, audit, training and investigation processes were not reviewed in the past six months, complete that review within three months and tell affected patients when snooping occurs.
exec: Insider misuse of patient records is now a regulatory priority, with a named executive expected to sign off and reply by November 27.
plain: The UK data watchdog told health service bosses to confirm personally that they can stop staff looking up records of patients they are not treating.

key_findings: The ICO wrote to over 200 senior health service leaders across the UK seeking personal assurance on unauthorised access to patient records.
It received and assessed over 300 reports of unauthorised access from health organisations between January 1 and mid-October 2026.
The ICO has prosecuted 16 healthcare staff for unlawfully accessing patient records in the last decade.
The letter, signed by chief executive Paul Arnold, sets a reply deadline of November 27, 2026.
recommendations: Control who can access patient records, and grant, review and remove access appropriately.
Monitor and audit systems to detect suspicious access.
Make sure all staff know what is expected and the consequences of unauthorised access.
Investigate suspected cases promptly, keep affected people informed and act where wrongdoing is found.
If no review was done in the past six months, complete one within three months.

summary: The ICO's chief executive wrote on November 12 to more than 200 senior UK health leaders asking for personal assurance that access to patient records is controlled, monitored and audited, that staff know the consequences of snooping and that suspected cases are investigated. The ICO assessed over 300 reports of unauthorised access between January 1 and mid-October 2026. Replies are due November 27; overdue reviews must be completed within three months.
title: ICO: UK health leaders told to give personal assurance on staff snooping in patient records

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Information Commissioner's Office document.
